name: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct
summary: Meta's smallest instruction-tuned Llama. Built for edge and CPU-only boxes where a reply in under a second matters more than depth.
strengths: Runs comfortably on CPU-only hardware and low-RAM VMs
Summarisation, rewriting, and short-form classification
Very low cost per request as a routing or triage model
limitations: Weak at multi-step reasoning and arithmetic
Not suitable for code generation
Hallucinates on knowledge-heavy questions

requirements.note: Comfortable on a laptop without a GPU.

name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
summary: The default Niyan local model. Good general instruction following at a size that still fits modest hardware, with a very long context window for document work.
strengths: Balanced general chat, summarisation, and extraction
128K context handles long documents and RAG payloads
Runs on CPU; comfortably fast on any modern GPU
limitations: Clearly behind 7B+ models on reasoning and code
Limited multilingual depth outside supported languages
Not a substitute for a frontier model on complex analysis

requirements.note: Usable on CPU; a 6 GB GPU gives a large speed-up.

name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
summary: The workhorse open-weight model. Strong all-round quality at a size most single-GPU servers can host, and the usual starting point for production self-hosting.
strengths: Reliable general assistant quality across most business tasks
Solid tool/function calling and structured output
Large ecosystem of fine-tunes and community tooling
limitations: Needs ~8 GB VRAM for comfortable GPU inference
Noticeably slower than 3B models on CPU
Behind dedicated coder models on programming tasks

requirements.note: CPU inference works but is slow; 8 GB VRAM recommended.

name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
summary: Meta's flagship open-weight model, delivering quality close to much larger closed models. A serious hardware commitment: multi-GPU or a very large unified-memory machine.
strengths: Frontier-adjacent quality on reasoning, analysis, and writing
Strong multilingual and instruction-following behaviour
Best open option when data must not leave your network
limitations: Requires ~40 GB+ of VRAM or unified memory
High latency and low throughput on modest hardware
Expensive to keep resident in memory

requirements.note: Plan for 2x 24 GB GPUs, one 48 GB GPU, or 64 GB+ unified memory.

name: Gemma 2 2B Instruct
summary: Google's compact Gemma. Punches above its weight on conversational quality, but the 8K context limits how much document you can feed it.
strengths: Strong chat quality relative to its size
Small download and fast cold start
Good for classification and short summarisation
limitations: Only 8K context — poor fit for large RAG payloads
Weak on maths and code
Gemma licence has use restrictions worth reviewing

requirements.note: Runs on CPU-only hosts.

name: Gemma 2 9B Instruct
summary: Mid-size Gemma with quality competitive with Llama 3.1 8B on general chat, at the cost of a much shorter context window.
strengths: Excellent conversational tone and instruction following
Competitive general knowledge for its size
Fits a single 12 GB GPU
limitations: 8K context is restrictive for retrieval workloads
Weaker code generation than Qwen or Llama equivalents
Licence restrictions worth legal review for commercial use

requirements.note: 8 GB VRAM is workable; 12 GB is comfortable.

name: Gemma 2 27B Instruct
summary: The largest Gemma 2. Approaches 70B-class quality on many chat benchmarks while staying on a single high-memory GPU.
strengths: High quality general reasoning and writing
Fits one 24 GB GPU at 4-bit quantization
Good alternative to 70B when VRAM is limited
limitations: 8K context remains the main constraint
Slow on CPU-only hosts
Large download and memory footprint

requirements.note: Targets a single 24 GB GPU.

name: Gemma 3 4B Instruct
summary: Gemma 3 fixes the context ceiling of Gemma 2 and adds image input. A strong small default when you need long documents or screenshots.
strengths: 128K context plus image understanding at a small size
Wide multilingual coverage
Runs on modest GPUs and capable laptops
limitations: Vision quality trails dedicated larger VLMs
Reasoning still limited by the 4B parameter count
Gemma licence restrictions apply

requirements.note: Image inputs increase memory use noticeably.

name: Gemma 3 12B Instruct
summary: Mid-size Gemma 3 with 128K context and vision. A good single-GPU choice when you want multimodal input without a 27B footprint.
strengths: Long context and image input on one mainstream GPU
Strong multilingual instruction following
Good document understanding including scans
limitations: Slower than text-only models of similar size
Needs 12 GB+ VRAM to be comfortable
Gemma licence restrictions apply

requirements.note: 12 GB VRAM minimum for image workloads.

name: Gemma 3 27B Instruct
summary: The top Gemma 3. Long context, image input, and quality that competes with much larger models — the strongest single-GPU multimodal option here.
strengths: Best multimodal quality in this catalog for one 24 GB GPU
128K context suits large RAG and document pipelines
Strong across reasoning, writing, and multilingual tasks
limitations: Needs 24 GB VRAM; impractical on CPU
Large download and slow cold start
Gemma licence restrictions apply

requirements.note: Targets a single 24 GB GPU.

name: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
summary: An Apache-2.0 licensed 7B that beats Llama 3.1 8B on most code and maths benchmarks. Often the best licence-to-quality trade-off at this size.
strengths: Permissive Apache 2.0 licence with no usage restrictions
Strong structured output and JSON adherence
Very good code and maths for a 7B model
limitations: English writing style can feel less natural than Llama
Long-context quality degrades well before the 128K limit
Needs ~8 GB VRAM for comfortable inference

requirements.note: 8 GB VRAM recommended.

name: Qwen2.5 14B Instruct
summary: The sweet spot of the Qwen2.5 line for a 16 GB GPU — a clear quality step over 7B without the memory cost of 32B.
strengths: Apache 2.0 with strong general and code performance
Fits a 16 GB GPU at 4-bit
Reliable structured output for agent workloads
limitations: Too large for CPU-only serving in practice
Long-context accuracy drops well under 128K
Slower cold start than 7B

requirements.note: 12-16 GB VRAM.

name: Qwen2.5 32B Instruct
summary: Near-70B quality on a single 24 GB GPU with an Apache 2.0 licence. A common production choice when 70B hardware is not available.
strengths: High general quality without multi-GPU hardware
Permissive licence for commercial deployment
Strong maths and code relative to size
limitations: Requires 24 GB VRAM at 4-bit quantization
Throughput drops sharply with concurrent users
20 GB download

requirements.note: Single 24 GB GPU or 32 GB+ unified memory.

name: Qwen2.5 Coder 7B Instruct
summary: A code-specialised Qwen2.5 that matches much larger general models on programming tasks. The default pick for a self-hosted coding assistant.
strengths: Excellent code generation, completion, and repair
Fill-in-the-middle support for editor integrations
Broad language coverage including SQL and shell
limitations: Noticeably weaker than general models on open chat
Not tuned for long-form writing or summarisation
Still needs review — generated code is not verified

requirements.note: 8 GB VRAM recommended.

name: Qwen2.5 Coder 32B Instruct
summary: The strongest open-weight coding model in this catalog, reported to rival frontier closed models on code benchmarks while staying self-hostable.
strengths: Frontier-class code generation and debugging
Handles large multi-file context
Apache 2.0 licence for commercial use
limitations: Needs a 24 GB GPU
Overkill for autocomplete — latency is high
General chat quality trails equivalent general models

requirements.note: Single 24 GB GPU or 32 GB+ unified memory.

name: Qwen3 8B
summary: Qwen3 introduces switchable thinking mode — the model can spend extra tokens reasoning before answering, or reply directly for latency-sensitive calls.
strengths: Toggle between fast answers and deliberate reasoning
Strong maths and logic for its size
Apache 2.0 licence
limitations: Thinking mode substantially increases latency and token cost
Reasoning traces can leak into output if not filtered
Newer model with a smaller fine-tune ecosystem

requirements.note: Thinking mode needs extra context headroom.

name: Qwen3 14B
summary: Mid-size Qwen3 with thinking mode. A good balance when you want reasoning quality without a 32B memory budget.
strengths: Strong structured reasoning and maths
Fits a 16 GB GPU
Apache 2.0 licence
limitations: Thinking mode is slow for interactive chat
Not practical on CPU
Token usage is higher than non-reasoning models

requirements.note: 12-16 GB VRAM.

name: Qwen3 32B
summary: The largest dense Qwen3 here. Best open reasoning quality that still fits one 24 GB GPU.
strengths: Top-tier open reasoning and maths performance
Single-GPU deployable at 4-bit
Apache 2.0 licence
limitations: High latency in thinking mode
24 GB VRAM required
Expensive to serve concurrently

requirements.note: Single 24 GB GPU or 32 GB+ unified memory.

name: Mistral 7B Instruct
summary: The model that established the 7B open-weight category. Now outperformed by newer 7Bs, but still fast, permissive, and extremely well supported.
strengths: Very fast inference and low memory use
Apache 2.0 licence
Huge ecosystem of fine-tunes and tooling
limitations: Behind Qwen2.5 and Llama 3.1 at the same size
Weak maths and code
32K context is modest by current standards

requirements.note: Runs acceptably on CPU.

name: Mistral NeMo 12B Instruct
summary: A joint Mistral/NVIDIA model with a 128K context and notably strong multilingual coverage, under a permissive licence.
strengths: Excellent multilingual performance including Indic languages
128K context under Apache 2.0
Good function calling support
limitations: Needs 12 GB VRAM to be comfortable
Maths and code trail Qwen equivalents
Slower than 7B models

requirements.note: 10-12 GB VRAM recommended.

name: Mixtral 8x7B Instruct
summary: A sparse mixture-of-experts model: it only activates ~13B parameters per token, so it runs faster than its size suggests — but all experts must still be in memory.
strengths: Quality near 70B dense models with faster token generation
Apache 2.0 licence
Strong multilingual European language support
limitations: Needs ~26 GB of memory even though only 13B is active
32K context only
Superseded by newer dense models at similar memory cost

requirements.note: All experts must be resident; memory use tracks total parameters.

name: Phi-3 Mini 3.8B Instruct
summary: Microsoft's small model trained on heavily curated 'textbook quality' data. Reasoning well above its parameter count, under a clean MIT licence.
strengths: Reasoning and maths far above its size class
MIT licence — no usage restrictions at all
Small enough for CPU and edge deployment
limitations: Narrow world knowledge from the curated training set
Weaker at open-ended creative writing
Can be overconfident on factual questions

requirements.note: Good CPU-only option when reasoning matters.

name: Phi-4 14B
summary: Microsoft's 14B reasoning-focused model. Reported to beat much larger models on maths and STEM benchmarks, under an MIT licence.
strengths: Outstanding maths and STEM reasoning for its size
MIT licence
Fits a 16 GB GPU
limitations: 16K context is small for document-heavy RAG
Less suited to conversational or creative work
Limited multilingual coverage

requirements.note: 12-16 GB VRAM.

name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill Qwen 7B
summary: A Qwen 7B distilled from DeepSeek-R1's reasoning traces. It writes out a chain of thought before answering, trading latency for accuracy on hard problems.
strengths: Maths and logic far above normal 7B models
MIT licence
Visible reasoning trace aids debugging and audit
limitations: Much slower — every answer includes a thinking phase
Reasoning tokens inflate cost and context use
Poor fit for short conversational replies

requirements.note: Allow extra context headroom for reasoning traces.

name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill Qwen 14B
summary: The mid-size R1 distillation. A clear accuracy step over the 7B on competition maths, still on a single 16 GB GPU.
strengths: Very strong maths and multi-step reasoning
MIT licence
Single-GPU deployable
limitations: High latency from extended reasoning
Not practical on CPU
Verbose output needs post-processing

requirements.note: 12-16 GB VRAM.

name: DeepSeek-R1 Distill Qwen 32B
summary: The largest R1 distillation that fits one 24 GB GPU. The best open maths and reasoning quality in this catalog.
strengths: Competition-level maths performance
MIT licence
Fits a single 24 GB GPU at 4-bit
limitations: Very high latency per answer
24 GB VRAM required
Unsuited to high-concurrency interactive use

requirements.note: Single 24 GB GPU or 32 GB+ unified memory.

name: Code Llama 7B Instruct
summary: Meta's original code model. Largely superseded by Qwen2.5-Coder, but still widely used in existing tooling and fine-tunes.
strengths: Well-supported fill-in-the-middle for editors
Mature ecosystem and integrations
Modest memory footprint
limitations: Well behind Qwen2.5-Coder on every code benchmark
16K context limits multi-file work
Llama 2 licence is more restrictive than Apache 2.0

requirements.note: Consider qwen2.5-coder:7b instead for new deployments.

name: Llama 3.2 Vision 11B
summary: Llama 3.2 with an image encoder. Handles document images, charts, and screenshots alongside text.
strengths: Document, chart, and diagram understanding
Long context for mixed text plus image workloads
Familiar Llama behaviour for text-only requests
limitations: Image processing adds significant latency and memory
Text-only quality is not better than Llama 3.1 8B
Licence restricts some uses — review before deploying

requirements.note: Image inputs push memory well above the text-only baseline.

name: LLaVA 1.6 7B
summary: A compact open vision-language model. Good for image captioning and simple visual Q&A where a larger VLM is not affordable.
strengths: Smallest practical vision model in this catalog
Apache 2.0 licence
Adequate for captioning and basic visual Q&A
limitations: Weak OCR and dense document understanding
Behind Gemma 3 and Llama Vision on accuracy
Short context for multi-image conversations

requirements.note: 8 GB VRAM recommended for image workloads.

name: Nomic Embed Text v1.5
summary: Niyan's default embedding model. 768 dimensions, 8K context, and small enough to keep resident permanently alongside a chat model.
strengths: Long 8192-token context for whole-document chunks
Tiny memory footprint — runs beside a chat model
Apache 2.0 licence
limitations: Not a chat model — embeddings only
English-centric; weaker on other languages
Changing embedding model requires re-indexing every collection

requirements.note: Create vector collections with size 768 to match.

name: mxbai-embed-large v1
summary: A higher-accuracy 1024-dimension embedding model. Better retrieval quality than nomic-embed-text, but a much shorter context means smaller chunks.
strengths: Stronger MTEB retrieval scores than nomic-embed-text
1024 dimensions capture finer semantic detail
Apache 2.0 licence
limitations: 512-token context forces small chunks
Larger vectors mean more storage and slower search
Switching to it requires re-indexing at size 1024

requirements.note: Create vector collections with size 1024 to match.

name: BGE-M3
summary: A multilingual embedding model covering 100+ languages with an 8K context. The right choice when your corpus is not English-only.
strengths: Strong multilingual retrieval across 100+ languages
8192-token context for large chunks
MIT licence
limitations: Larger and slower than nomic-embed-text
1024 dimensions increase vector storage cost
Requires re-indexing when switching to it

requirements.note: Create vector collections with size 1024 to match.
